I am a 36-year-old farmer in Oromia with some schooling, and I manage nearly seven hectares in total, though this barley plot is rented. The rains have been decent lately, so I will plant barley here using improved seed I got from the agricultural office last year—it gives better yield than local seed if the season is good. I will put some DAP and urea on this plot because the soil is getting tired, but I cannot afford too much since it is rented land and I must save money for my other plots. My family will do most of the planting, weeding, and harvesting, but during the busy weeks I will hire a few day laborers from the village to help us finish on time. We do not irrigate here—there is no canal or pump—and chemicals for pests are too expensive for barley, so we will weed by hand and pray the birds and frost stay away.
